title: Religion design document's data model and numbers are out of date
what: The religion design document still describes the old fields (a 'chief' deity and a 1.15 hold multiplier); the code now uses patron fields, resists 0.35 of each downward step, and adds legitimacy, a sink, patron falls, suppression ticks, a push margin and standing hysteresis (a dead band against flicker). Host: docs/RELIGION_REWORK.md:93-101, :204-207 vs src/domain/worldPulse/religionState.js:45-85 and worldState.js:272-280.
why: Anyone, including the map, who builds from the document gets wrong field names and wrong numbers.
when: Bring the document up to the code (the note records the code as having outrun it).

title: Global rank is by patron seats, not by adherents
what: The design document ranks deities by adherents; the code counts only the settlements that seat the deity as patron. Host: docs/RELIGION_REWORK.md §2.7 vs the code the note cites in its §4.2.
why: A legend ordered by 'number of believers' would show a number the host never computes.

title: Patron is the top share overall, not the top of the top three
what: The document says the leading deity is the top share among the top three; the code takes the top share overall, and the top three appear only in the contest. Host: docs/RELIGION_REWORK.md:32-34.
why: Small; a reader would expect a rule the code does not run.

title: Deity temper is derived, but comments say it is stored
what: The document derives a deity's niche from a stored temperament field; the code derives temper from the deity's two axes, and two code comments still say 'stored verbatim'. Host: docs/RELIGION_REWORK.md:29, :37; src/domain/worldPulse/cultImpositionApply.js:22-26; src/domain/worldPulse/religiousContest.js:224.
why: A reader would trust a stored value that no engine read uses.
when: Fix the document and the two comments.

title: 'Every world is born with a pantheon' is retired but still stated in six places
what: Generation no longer creates a starting pantheon (the latent pantheon was deleted), but the 'latent in every seed' claim survives in user copy and code headers. Host: docs/RELIGION_REWORK.md:180-185; docs/PHASE4_FAITH_DELTA.md §4; src/components/compendium/PantheonActivationStrip.jsx:6-9; src/copy/deityAuthoring.js:74, :105-106; src/components/settlement/faithPanelModel.js:12-14; src/domain/display/publicSafe.js:73-75; header of supabase migration 128.
why: Users and developers are told a fresh world has gods when it has none; a faith lens on a born world is empty.
when: Remove the claim from the listed files (the note records it as retired).

title: Design documents miss the split into a local lane and a spread lane
what: The religion document presents carriers, prevalence and occupation entry as the whole model without saying they run only in the spread lane; the Phase 4 document says piety is absent (it is built) and puts realm-wide deity politics in the spread lane, while the pantheon ranking advances on local activity. Host: docs/RELIGION_REWORK.md §2.4-§2.6; docs/PHASE4_FAITH_DELTA.md §1.3, §1.9; src/domain/worldPulse/pulseKernel.js:1704.
why: A reader would think spread runs everywhere and that piety does not exist.
when: Mark those passages spread-only and update §1.3 and §1.9.

title: Code says faith never crosses a settlement boundary unless spread is on; it does
what: Two code comments say spread is the only gated faith dynamic and otherwise faith never crosses a settlement boundary; in the default preset (RR, realistic_regional) faith prescription, the fracture spread, tolerance drift, faith-weighted relief and (on a canonized world) faith-weighted contraband all cross boundaries, and the Living-World gate (a per-campaign DM switch) can light spread itself. Host: src/domain/worldPulse/simulationRules.js:90-100; src/domain/worldPulse/religiousContest.js:24-33.
why: A map built on the comment would draw the default world as having no faith pressure between towns.
when: Correct both comments (the note's §6.1, §6.10, §6.11, §7.4, §7.10 carry the evidence).

title: Fracture and conversion said to travel 'along religious_authority'
what: A comment says the fracture spreads along the religious-authority channel; the code declares three channels. And 'conversion spreads along religious_authority' confuses the drawn faith front (a record, not a carrier) with the creed's real path. Host: src/domain/worldPulse/religiousContest.js:10-12.
why: The map would draw the wrong link type as the path of a schism or conversion.

title: Conversion reads distance but not travel delay
what: The spatial design document says conversion inherits both distance and travel latency; the code applies distance only. The couplings document's 'faith spreads at carrier reach' omits the built distance weakening altogether. Host: docs/PHASE55_SPATIAL_ENGINE_DESIGN.md §3; docs/DESIGN_FP_COUPLINGS.md; src/domain/worldPulse/religiousContest.js:365-376.
why: A map showing faith arriving 'after N weeks' would invent a delay the host does not have.

title: Three faith files claim to be unused; they are wired
what: faithField.js's header says nothing calls it (called since F4c); customContentSchema.js says 'no mechanical consumer'; faithWitnessSource.js says its funnel is absent though the catalog admits it (still no caller). Host: faithField.js header (path not given in this section); customContentSchema.js:241-242, :297-298; faithWitnessSource.js:16-30.
why: Developers may delete or ignore live code.

title: 'Five causes' of a patron fall: four ship
what: Three design documents say a patron can fall for five causes; the code has four. Host: docs/DESIGN_FP_ARCH_WF.md:270, :418; docs/DESIGN_FP_FAITH.md J-WF-5 :1498; docs/DESIGN_FP_ARCHITECTURE.md:1991; src/domain/worldPulse/patronFall.js:76.
why: A map legend of fall causes would list one that never happens.

title: The Schism realm arc does not exist
what: The faith design document says a Schism realm arc exists; it does not. Host: docs/DESIGN_FP_FAITH.md:1327.
why: A time scrub would look for a dated event the host never makes.

title: 'God's Abandonment' still ships despite the rename ruling
what: The owner's ruling OD-FC-8 (a rename) is not applied; the old 'God's Abandonment' text still ships.
why: Players see wording the owner ruled out.
when: Apply OD-FC-8 (listed again as awaiting application in §10.3).

title: 'The faithful walk the roads' headline has no mechanic
what: The Ascendancy headline says the faithful walk the roads; nothing moves them.
why: Players read about travellers who are not simulated; an encounter map would have no host fact to show.
when: The note records the gap; no specific fix given.

title: Believed devotion ruling not applied
what: OD-FC-7 (light believed devotion in three presets) was ruled but is not applied at revision 81f1cd96.
why: Player-side 'what people believe about faith' stays dark where the owner said it should be lit.

title: Which lane carries pilgrims and legates is recorded three different ways
what: The faith design says WF-2 (the designed pilgrim and named-mover feature) rides SPREAD plus SP-1; the WF architecture document says SPREAD plus the errand spine; pilgrims' purpose class was corrected from religious to personal (J-EM-6); a slice brief put pilgrims and legates in the Wayfare document, which never mentions them (they live in the faith design and in the envoy errand vocabulary). Host: docs/DESIGN_FP_FAITH.md §3; docs/DESIGN_FP_ARCH_WF.md:190; docs/DESIGN_FP_ARCH_WY.md; src/domain/worldPulse/envoyErrandVocabulary.js:322-335.
why: Encounter maps that place pilgrims depend on which system owns them; today the documents disagree.
when: Reconcile the documents on one lane and one home.

title: Pilgrimage right drafted ungated though it cannot form without WF-2
what: The WF architecture document says the pilgrimage_right grant cannot form without WF-2; the draft lens drafts it ungated. Host: docs/DESIGN_FP_ARCH_WF.md:499.
why: A peace or treaty view could offer a grant the engine cannot produce.
when: Gate the draft on WF-2 (implied by the ARCH_WF line the note cites).

title: Missionary access: share mover or gate
what: The grammar document said missionary_access 'moves believer-share bands'; the faith design says it is 'a gate, never a share'; already clarified at docs/DESIGN_FP_GRAMMAR.md:868.
why: Settled in the document; listed for completeness.

title: The GR-6 temple arm can never be reached
what: Under the one-finder law the GR-6 temple arm is unreachable. Host: docs/DESIGN_FP_GRAMMAR.md:1290.
why: Designed behaviour that cannot happen.
when: The note records it; no fix given.

title: One-writer rule broken by the traditions nudge
what: A ruling says one writer family owns the value; the traditions nudge still writes it, and the code cure is owed. Host: docs/DESIGN_FP_COHERENCE_FOLD.md:267.
why: Two writers can make a value drift silently.

title: The generation-time tithe is covered by no ruling
what: The tithe has four sources, ruled to be one flow with two ends; the static tithe written at generation is not mentioned by any ruling (note §7.4).
why: An undecided money flow; a map showing tithe would not know which source is true.

title: Stale comment on the 'full' information mode
what: A normaliser comment on info mode 'full' is stale (see alignment-31a for the host lines).
why: Misleads a reader about whether beliefs run in FS.

title: Design documents cite superseded line numbers
what: The WF architecture document (R4) and the couplings document cite old line numbers for the kernel mounts, the carriers and mediation. Host: docs/DESIGN_FP_ARCH_WF.md R4; docs/DESIGN_FP_COUPLINGS.md.
why: Readers land on the wrong code.

title: 'LivingWorldGates still writes the legacy key' is stale
what: The spatial design says the Living-World gate writes only the legacy key; since CL-0 it writes both keys. Host: docs/PHASE55_SPATIAL_ENGINE_DESIGN.md:1588-1589.
why: Misleads anyone deciding which flag to read.

title: Regional graph header still reserves propagation for 'a future tier'
what: The regional graph header says active propagation is for a future tier; it already happens (note §7.10.3). Host: regionalGraph.js:19-22.
why: Readers think the graph is passive.

title: The 'War & faith' switch cannot hide faith; the Faith door has no map chip
what: Turning off the 'War & faith' layer leaves the faith fronts drawn (they belong to the Relationships layer), and the Herald's Faith door offers no map-lens chip. Host: src/components/map/WarFaithMapOverlay.jsx:1-26; src/components/map/LayersPanel.jsx:238-242; src/components/map/HeraldBody.jsx:282-291.
why: The switch's name promises control the user does not get.
when: Open question in §10.3: should the switch govern the faith front.

title: Pantheon panel shows a deity weaker than the engine treats it
what: The panel's strength bar uses the earned ranking tier; the engine converts at the higher of authored and earned tier, so an authored-major deity with one seat shows as a 35% cult but converts at 0.95. Host: src/components/map/PantheonPanel.jsx:185-186, :216.
why: Wrong number on screen; a lens copying the panel would repeat it.
when: The note records it; the fix implied is to display the tier the engine uses.

title: Faith-front style comment says 'allied/trade edge'; it can be a war front
what: The edge style comment says the faith front lies along an allied or trade edge; it can lie along a war front. Host: src/components/map/relationshipEdgeStyle.js:60-61.
why: Misleads the map designer about what the purple line means.

title: Activation strip demands the old spread flag
what: The pantheon activation strip's 'dynamics' milestone accepts the legacy spread flag, though the local lane and the ranking need no flag. Host: src/components/compendium/PantheonActivationStrip.jsx:45-49.
why: The DM is told dynamics are off when local dynamics run.
when: The note records it; no fix given.

title: 'Patron-less town' text is effectively unreachable
what: The DS-FTH-2 prose is mounted only for a premium viewer with no embed, who gets no Faith tab; the desk's header admits an untested direction. Host: src/components/new/tabs/WarFaithDesk.jsx:272-292, :32-43; FaithTab.jsx:227, :284-309; src/components/OutputContainer.jsx:511-514.
why: Authored content nobody sees.
when: The note records it; no fix given.

title: War verbs still labelled 'coming soon'
what: AssignDeityFromMap says the war verbs are coming soon. Host: src/components/map/AssignDeityFromMap.jsx:14-16.
why: Stale user-facing promise.

title: Two components disagree on whether the faith tab hides itself
what: PantheonPanel says the tab self-hides; RealmInspector says no door does. Host: src/components/map/PantheonPanel.jsx:9-11; RealmInspector.jsx:83-87.
why: Developers cannot tell which behaviour is intended.

title: Faith panel falls back to a field snapshots no longer carry
what: faithPanelModel falls back to 'portfolio', which deity snapshots no longer carry. Host: src/components/settlement/faithPanelModel.js.
why: The fallback silently yields nothing.
when: The note records it; no fix given.

title: A cult imposed after seeding is never admitted
what: A post-seed IMPOSE_CULT action is never admitted to the pantheon (note §3.11).
why: A DM action appears to do nothing.

title: A conversion's recorded source is the convert itself
what: The conversion receipt names the convert as its own source (note §6.7).
why: The map cannot say where a conversion came from.
when: §9.6 item 5 implies a host ask: put the strongest carrier source on the receipt.

title: A DM re-assign records no win or loss
what: When a DM re-assigns a patron, no win/loss is banked to the ranking (note §3.6).
why: The global ranking misses DM-made changes.
when: The note records it; no fix given.

title: Faith fronts are never retired
what: Once a faith front (a confirmed religious_authority channel, the purple dashed line) is minted it stays, even after its carrier ends (note §6.3).
why: The map shows old fronts as if live; a lens must style them as historic.
when: §9.6 item 5 implies a host ask: retire mints when the carrier ends; §10.3 asks the owner.

title: Hostile war fronts carry faith hardest
what: War-front links carry faith at 0.72, stronger than any friendly link (note §6.2).
why: Enemies convert each other fastest; a map drawing faith along friendly links would be wrong.

title: Any link of any status counts as a prevalence neighbour
what: neighbourIdsOf counts any link, including rival, criminal and dormant ones, as a prevalence neighbour (note §6.5).
why: Faith prevalence leaks along links that should not carry it.
when: The note records it; no fix given.

title: Two faith-reach calculations disagree
what: The spread lane's reach and buildFaithReach differ (one gated, one ungated; note §6.11 and §9.5 item 3).
why: Two different 'reach' numbers for the same deity; a lens must pick one and say which.
when: The note records it; no fix given.

title: History text uses generic deity names and named Christian orders
what: History text still uses generic deity names and named Christian orders (note §2.5).
why: Breaks the setting's own deity names.
when: The note records it; no fix given.

title: Clearing a patron leaves a stale pantheon
what: A patron clear leaves the settlement's pantheon and ledgers stale (note §3.11).
why: The map would show a faith mix for a town with no patron.
when: §10.3 asks whether SET_PRIMARY_DEITY with no deity should clear the pantheon.

title: A demotion leaves too many deities in a pantheon
what: A demotion leaves an over-capacity pantheon (note §3.11).
why: More deities shown than the tier allows.
when: §10.3 asks whether a demotion should trim it.

title: Rival-cult blame names cults never admitted
what: rivalCult blames cults the pantheon never admitted (note §3.11).
why: Receipts name a cult the town does not hold.
when: The note records it; no fix given.

title: A suggested candidate could pin a faith front at 'suggested'
what: A suggested discovery candidate could pin a pulse mint at 'suggested' status [INFERRED in the note] (note §6.3).
why: A front could stay unconfirmed and undrawn.
when: The note records it as inferred; no fix given.

what: The 'Dominant faith' tile names the deity by the tail of its id, not its name (note §7.10.11). Host: src/components/map/RealmDashboard.jsx (tile at :65-77, :368-371 per §9.1).
why: Users see a code string instead of a god's name.
when: The note records it; no fix given.

title: Research seats' disagreement resolved (research record)
what: Faith-field import is wired (dormant by data); hostile labels are not carriers but their war_front channels are.

title: Wayfare ruling to delete the deployment arrows is not applied
what: The Wayfare document ruled the deployment arrows deleted; the 'War & faith' overlay still draws them. Host: docs/DESIGN_FP_ARCH_WY.md:56-58, :1653-1660; src/components/map/WarFaithMapOverlay.jsx:98-105.
why: The world map draws something the owner ruled out.

title: Town buildings reserve a patron look but never read the patron
what: The building grammar reserves patron alignment and an emblem, but hard-codes both alignments to 0.5 and makes the emblem from the scene, not from any deity. Host: src/domain/townScene/buildingProfiles.js:331-336; src/domain/townMap/arch/params.js:18-31. (Same seam as alignment-17e.)
why: Town maps cannot show a temple's god.
when: The note records it; the town fabric's worship ladder is designed only and ruled out of FP.

title: Pilgrims, missionaries and inquisitors are not simulated as travellers
what: The only pilgrim maths is a deity-blind host lift that discards who came; 'missionize' is a trust nudge; WF-2's season and named movers are unbuilt and their spine (the errand system) is dark. WF-2's design (season from draw x believed devotion x route viability, road danger, 52-week feasts, interceptable errands with a return leg) is the spec a lens should mirror.
why: Faith encounters on an encounter map would be invention until WF-2 lands.
when: Build WF-2 if faith travellers are wanted on encounter maps; until then the map shows none.

title: Should a new world be born with any deity (FPQ-62)?
what: No deity exists until a premium DM authors one.
why: Every faith lens is empty on fresh worlds.

title: Should the default preset turn on faith spread?
what: faithSpreadEnabled is off in the default preset (RR) unless a DM lights it per campaign.
why: Without it, conversion between settlements does not exist in the preset worlds are born into.

title: Should faith fronts carry the deity and source, and retire when the link ends?
what: Fronts carry no deity id and no source and are never retired; §9.6 item 5 frames this as a host ask: put the deity id and strongest carrier source on the front and on the conversion receipt, and retire fronts when the carrier ends.
why: Decides whether a lens can draw present fronts or only historic ones, and whether it can name a conversion's source.

title: Should hostile relationships carry faith at 0.72, the strongest carrier?
what: See faith-25e.
why: Shapes every faith-pressure map.

title: Should the faith contest read seasons, travel time or sea lanes; should realm piety be weighted?
what: Only the parked ripple and moral founding read a season; realm piety is not size- or distance-weighted. A sea route as a cheap faith carrier would be new host simulation (§9.6 item 9).
why: Decides whether faith movement can ever follow geography.

title: Should the map render the host's religious hierarchy?
what: mapProfile's regionalAuthority output (religious-superior and pilgrimage-centre links) says 'the map should render' it; nothing consumes it.
why: A host fact the map is asked to draw and does not.
when: Owner to decide whether the map module's lens renders it.

title: Should clearing a patron clear the pantheon; should a demotion trim it?
what: See faith-25i and faith-25j.
why: Stale faith mixes on the map.

title: Should 'War & faith' govern the faith front; should players ever see DM-only fronts?
what: See faith-19; fronts are DM-only by default and dropped from published maps.
why: Audience and switch behaviour of the purple lines.

title: May the map derive a pilgrim catchment or place holy sites?
what: The host keeps no pilgrim catchment (it discards the draw) and no positioned holy sites; settlement labels exist. Positioned sites would be map-side facts needing an owner ruling and, to matter, host adoption (§9.6 item 6).
why: Decides whether encounter and religion maps may show pilgrim areas and shrines.

title: Is the post-seed cult admission intended or a defect?
what: See faith-25a.

title: Two faith rulings await application
what: OD-FC-7 (believed devotion) and OD-FC-8 (the rename; the attributed edit). See faith-12 and faith-11c.

title: Map's own: religion lens reads only host facts listed in the needs table
what: Patron, mix, piety, ranking, fronts, carriers, receipts, distance weights, flags; audience notes per row.

title: Map's own: show mixtures, not borders; label recomputed pressure as derived
what: Patron colour with share pie, restyled historic fronts, crisis ripple, tension marks, seat footprint, scrub needs map-side snapshots.

title: Map's own: never draw pilgrims, missionaries, positioned holy places or latent deities as host facts
what: Nor recover a conversion's source, nor show DM-only fronts or suppressed creeds to players.

title: Map's own: open in a 'still pantheons' mode when spread is off; read resolved campaign flags
what: Default preset has nothing moving unless the DM lights it.

title: Map's own: 'pressure along carrier links', not 'flows along routes'
what: Carriers are diplomacy and garrison links; geography only weakens on canonized worlds.

title: Map's own: show the host's culture resistance term, do not add one; player view is narrow
what: Receptivity is the host's resistance; believed faith only in DC, LR, FS on canon.
